findings.evidence: The only application theorem found for `peterWeylTraceEquiv` is `peterWeylTraceEquiv_symm_apply` at lines 62–70; lines 117–126 provide equivariance but still do not identify the coordinates of an arbitrary input.
findings.fix: Add a forward-application lemma expressing each coordinate as the inner product of `f` with the corresponding transposed `peterWeylBlockOrthonormalBasis`/normalized trace coefficient, and mark the pointwise normal-form lemma `@[simp]`.
findings.issue: `peterWeylTraceEquiv` characterizes only `symm`; there is no theorem computing `(peterWeylTraceEquiv h f) i (j,k)`, although coordinate extraction is the defining elimination API of this decomposition.

summary: The new Hilbert-sum equivalence lacks a usable characterization of its forward map, leaving consumers unable to extract Fourier/Peter–Weyl coordinates without unfolding Mathlib internals.
